question: Why do the two completed-turn findings have no real case in this corpus?

P0047.reader: `scan` asks whether a completed turn answered anyone by looking at the last step for text or a tool call (core/answer.ts, P-0044).
P0047.host_half: The adapter decides to end a turn on block count: `mapStopReason` treats `message.content.length === 0` as empty, so a turn whose only assistant content is a reasoning block ends as a normal `completed` stop. P-0047 names that consequence; it does not fix the adapter.
P0047.source: quoted in docs/patches/P-0047-completed-without-answer.md (host file and line cited there)

P0052.reader: `scan` also counts a completed turn whose last step still carries a tool-call block; `explain` prints TOOLCALL (P-0052).
P0052.host_half: The loop only ends a step with tool calls when a tool result carries `concludesTurn` (dsh-agent-loop/src/agent.ts:592-603), and the chat UI renders only a final step with no tool-call block as an answer (dsh-client-ui-chat .../turn-process.ts:160-161). The two rules can disagree, which is the upstream #12741 shape.
P0052.source: quoted in docs/patches/P-0052-completed-on-tool-call.md (host file and line cited there)

not_proven: no user on this machine hit either shape in the measured corpus; both rules are exercised by probes, not by a real session
the host source is quoted from the patch documents that read it at the cited line, not re-downloaded by this recorder
a different host, provider route or UI build may produce the shape; absence here is not absence everywhere
